title: Canonical kernel and degree projections of a coproduct quotient
statement: Given j:Z→X a closed immersion and the graded algebra coproduct data A [lem-sc-tensor-graded-algebra-data], the canonical kernel sequence of its underlying quotient p is short exact. It admits degree projection morphisms to the kernel sequences of eta_d [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] and inclusions k_d:ker eta_d→ker p exhibiting ker p as their sheaf coproduct. The inclusion squares commute, the diagonal kernel and quotient composites are identities, and the off-diagonal kernel composites vanish. No square-zero or invertibility assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 09MS, coherent-equation-ses and its direct sum; canonical construction before cohomology

proof.text: The closed-immersion unit in each degree is epi; adjunction uniqueness transfers this to tensorGradedUnit. Using the target coproduct universal property, the quotient p is epi.

The module category is Grothendieck abelian, so coproducts are exact. Apply Mathlib colim.map_mono' and colim.exact_mapShortComplex to the pointwise kernel sequences. Their colimit is a kernel fork for p, whose unique isomorphism with the canonical kernel transports the kernel coproduct.

Define the degree projections by coproduct descent with identity in their own degree and zero otherwise. Check the quotient squares on inclusions, induce maps of kernels, and cancel kernel inclusions to prove the diagonal and orthogonality equations.

In an abelian category with exact coproducts the coproduct of kernels is the kernel of a coproduct of morphisms
